Generate a travel time map

Source: R/traveltime.R
traveltime.Rd

traveltime() generates a map of the travel time (in minutes) to the nearest facility, based on the input facilities, area of interest, and travel mode.

See the friction() function for details on how the friction layer is generated.

Usage

traveltime(
  facilities,
  bb_area,
  mode = "walk",
  dowscaling_model_type = NULL,
  res_output = 100,
  cache = FALSE,
  file = NULL,
  roads = NULL,
  road_speeds = default_road_speeds()
)

Arguments

facilities

A sf object with the existing facilities (POINT geometries).

bb_area

A sf object with the polygon(s) of the area of interest.

mode

(optional) A character string indicating the mode of transport. Options are "fastest" and "walk" (default: "walk").

  • For "fastest": The friction layer accounts for multiple modes of transport, including walking and driving. At the native resolution, it is the Malaria Atlas Project (2015) Global Travel Speed Friction Surface.

  • For "walk": The friction layer accounts only for walking speeds and is based on the Malaria Atlas Project (2020) Global Walking Only Friction Surface.

dowscaling_model_type

Deprecated and ignored. The friction surface is no longer downscaled with a statistical model (see Details).

res_output

(optional) A positive integerish number indicating the spatial resolution of the friction raster (and of the analysis), in meters. See Details (default: 100).

cache

(optional) A logical flag indicating whether to cache downloaded data (friction surface of the area, road network) on disk and reuse it in later calls. It also enables a fallback to a one-time download of the global friction surface (~730 MB) when the Malaria Atlas Project service is unavailable. See Details of friction() (default: FALSE).

file

(optional) A character string indicating the path to a local Malaria Atlas Project friction surface raster file, used instead of downloading it: the walking-only surface, except with mode = "fastest" and res_output >= 1000, where it is the travel speed surface (default: NULL).

roads

(optional) A sf object with the road network (LINESTRING or MULTILINESTRING geometries), used when mode = "fastest" and res_output < 1000. It must have either a speed column with speeds in km/h, or a highway column with OpenStreetMap road classes, which are converted to speeds with road_speeds. If NULL, the road network is downloaded from OpenStreetMap (default: NULL).

road_speeds

(optional) A named numeric vector with the speed (km/h) of each OpenStreetMap road class (highway tag). Road classes not in road_speeds are ignored (default: default_road_speeds()).

Value

An invisible list of class traveltime with the following elements:

  • travel_time: A RasterLayer object with the travel time (in minutes) to the nearest facility.

  • friction: A list with the outputs of the friction() function.

Details

All facilities within the extent of the friction surface (i.e., the bounding box of bb_area) are used as sources, including those located just outside the boundary of bb_area, since they can still serve demand within it. The resulting travel time map is masked to bb_area. Cells that cannot be reached from any facility (e.g., cells with no friction data, such as open water) have an infinite travel time.

See also

Other travel time functions: default_road_speeds(), friction(), traveltime_plot(), traveltime_stats()

Examples

# Offline example with a bundled copy of the walking surface for Naples
friction_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "naples-friction-walk.tif",
  package = "locationallocation"
)

traveltime_data <-
  naples_fountains |>
  traveltime(
    bb_area = naples_shape,
    res_output = 1000,
    file = friction_file
  )
#> ℹ Using user-provided friction data file
#> ✔ Using user-provided friction data file [547ms]
#> 
#> ℹ Computing transition matrix and geocorrection
#> ✔ Computing transition matrix and geocorrection [36ms]
#> 
#> ℹ Computing travel time map
#> ✔ Computing travel time map [13ms]
#> 

traveltime_data
#> Travel time map
#> • Travel time (minutes): median 8.44, max 53.18
#> • Unreachable cells: 0 of 231
#> • Resolution: 0.00833 and 0.00833 degrees (15 x 26 cells)

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Download the friction surface (requires an internet connection)
traveltime_data <-
  naples_fountains |>
  traveltime(bb_area = naples_shape, mode = "walk", res_output = 100)
} # }
